summary: A price cut is a landed-price decrease, and market-level aggregates stay withheld below the five-car cohort floor.
reason: Any nonzero movement was counted as a cut, so increase-only cars failed --never-cut. Aggregate degradation also reported median/worst/best on 1-4 cars, presenting an undersized sample as a market result.
validated_outcome: Unit and command tests: increase-only paths emit zero cuts and survive stale --never-cut; degradation with n=3 withholds aggregates and n=5 reports them.
